Create a college and invite its admin.

No tokens are granted here — that is a separate, audited action with a reason

created it and why.
Soft-delete. Hard deletion is a separate purge job after the retention period.

confirmation from the college, done out of band. Students can never self-add a domain,
which is what stops a lookalike like `indoreinstitute-edu.com`.
A college admin sets their own password from the invite link.

CreateOrderRequest.title: CreateOrderRequest
CreateOrderRequest.description: Only a plan code. The server looks up price and token count.

EnrollCollegeRequest.title: EnrollCollegeRequest
EnrollCollegeRequest.description:
Creates the college and *invites* its admin.

No password field: we never set a password on someone else's behalf. The invited
college admin receives a one-time link and chooses their own.

GrantTokensRequest.title: GrantTokensRequest
GrantTokensRequest.description: Admin-only. A reason is mandatory — it lands in the audit log and the ledger.

OAuthExchangeRequest.title: OAuthExchangeRequest
OAuthExchangeRequest.description:
Exchanges the one-time code from the OAuth redirect for a real token.

The callback no longer puts a JWT in the redirect URL, where it would land in browser
history, the Referer header and proxy logs.

PaymentStatusResponse.title: PaymentStatusResponse
PaymentStatusResponse.description:
What the client-side callback gets: status only.

Tokens are granted by the webhook, so this endpoint cannot be replayed for credit.

ProctoringBatchRequest.title: ProctoringBatchRequest
ProctoringBatchRequest.description: Events are batched over HTTP every few seconds instead of streamed.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest
RegisterRequest.description: Note the absence of a `role` field — roles are assigned by the server only.

StartInterviewRequest.title: StartInterviewRequest
StartInterviewRequest.description:
Exactly one of `jd_id` or `custom_jd_id`. No `student_id` — that comes from the
bearer token, so an interview can no longer be attributed to another student.

SubmitTurnRequest.title: SubmitTurnRequest
SubmitTurnRequest.description:
One answer. Replaces the WebSocket `turn_complete` message (PLAN.md §0.1).

`turn_id` is generated by the client and makes submission idempotent: a retry after a
dropped connection returns the original next question instead of burning a turn.
